# Opt-in focus streak (focusSheen prop) (and 1 more)

This request comes from a conversation with the developer about their app.
Anything marked suspected or not checked is a guess: confirm it in the code before building on it.

## What this is about
The developer likes the one-time light streak that the split button's chevron plays on mount. They want a similar streak as an opt-in feature on any ZestButton, regular or split. It should play across the whole button when it gets keyboard focus, and the host should also be able to trigger it from code. This helps users see which button has focus on screens with many components.

## What to build or fix

### 1. Opt-in focus streak (focusSheen prop) (confirmed)
Add an opt-in boolean prop (working name `focusSheen`, default off). When on, a light streak sweeps across the whole button when it gets keyboard focus, using `:focus-visible` (not plain `:focus`, so mouse clicks do not trigger it). Direction: starts at the top-right corner and sweeps to the bottom-left at about 45 degrees. This is the assistant's reading of 'about 45 degrees from top right', and the developer was asked to correct it if wrong but did not. Duration about 0.6s, play once per focus arrival. The existing focus ring stays the main focus signal, and the streak is decoration only. Regular button: use a `::after` layer on the button itself. The base `.button` already has position:relative and overflow:hidden, so it clips the streak. Regular buttons use no ::before or ::after today, so there is no clash. Split button: the streak covers the whole control (both segments), not per segment. Put position:relative and overflow:hidden on `.splitButtonContainer` and add a streak layer to it, triggered with `:has(:focus-visible)` (or `:focus-within`) on the wrapper so focus on either segment plays one sweep. The wrapper has no border-radius today, so give it a radius matching the buttons' outer corners so the clip looks right. The dropdown menu will not be clipped, because it renders in a Radix Portal outside the wrapper. When the focus streak is active on a split button, turn off the chevron's own mount streak (`.dropdownTrigger::before`) so two streaks do not play together. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling the streak. Colour: white at about 65% suits solid buttons. It would barely show on outline, text and dashed styles, so decide whether the first version covers only solid styles or adjusts the colour per style.

Evidence:

- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:588-600
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:151-153 (.button position:relative, overflow:hidden)
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:179-182 (focus ring uses :focus-visible)
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:495-498 (.splitButtonContainer inline-flex, no position or overflow)
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:653-656 (reduced-motion disables mount streak)
- UI/ZestButton.tsx:418 (regular button uses the shared button class)
- UI/ZestDropdownMenu.tsx:67-68 (chevron trigger uses the shared button class)
- UI/ZestButton.tsx:453-469 (split wrapper)
- UI/ZestDropdownMenu.tsx:85-87 (menu rendered in a Radix Portal)

### 2. Programmatic streak trigger (sheenTrigger prop) (confirmed)
Add a prop (working name `sheenTrigger`, a number or key) so the host can play the streak from code. Each change of its value plays one streak. The first value on mount does NOT play (the assistant's default, which the developer did not contradict). It works independently of `focusSheen`, so it plays even when `focusSheen` is off. It uses the same streak layer and keyframes as the focus streak. On a split button it sweeps the whole control through the wrapper layer. It plays on disabled buttons too (assistant's default, not contradicted). It is still disabled under prefers-reduced-motion, with no override. The developer chose a changing-value prop over a ref handle or a boolean prop. ZestButton has no forwardRef, so adding a ref would be a bigger API change. Replay needs the animation to restart each time. The suggested approach is to re-key the streak layer on the trigger value, or to remove and re-add the class. This has not been tested in this code, so verify that repeated triggers replay after building.

Evidence:
- UI/ZestButton.tsx:170 (plain React.FC, no forwardRef or useImperativeHandle)
- Styles/ZestButton.module.css:572-586 (existing streak is CSS-only, so there is no replay logic today)

## Not part of this
- A provider-level default for the focus streak in ZestButtonConfigProvider (left out of the first version).
- A ref handle such as ref.current.sheen(), and adding forwardRef to ZestButton.
- Changing the existing mount streak on the chevron, apart from turning it off on split buttons when the new streak is active.
- Triggering the streak on mouse click (plain :focus).

## Not settled yet (do not treat as fact)
- Direction: the assistant read '45 degrees from top right' as top-right to bottom-left. The developer did not explicitly confirm this.
- Should the first value of sheenTrigger on mount play a streak? The default is no, and the developer did not confirm.
- Should a trigger play on disabled or busy buttons? The default is yes, and the developer did not confirm.
- Does the first version cover only solid button styles, or adjust the streak colour for outline, text and dashed styles with light backgrounds?
- Exact duration (about 0.6s proposed) and the name of the props are working choices, not confirmed.
- Whether replay on repeated sheenTrigger changes works with the chosen re-key approach has not been tested.

## Requirements agreed in the conversation

The developer and the assistant already agreed these while talking. Build on them; do not ask again what they settle.

- **R1**: A button can be configured to play the diagonal light-streak effect when it gains focus. The option is off by default and is turned on per button.
  - Done when: With the option off, focusing the button shows no streak.
  - Done when: With the option on, focusing the button plays the streak.
  - Done when: Both a regular button and a split button can have the option turned on.
- **R2**: The streak is a diagonal band at about 45 degrees that starts from the top-right area of the button and sweeps across the whole button, clipped to the button's shape.
  - Done when: The band is visibly diagonal at about 45 degrees and travels from the top-right towards the opposite side.
  - Done when: No part of the streak is visible outside the button's edges.
- **R3**: When a split button has the option enabled, focusing either segment plays one streak that sweeps across the whole split control, not one streak per segment.
  - Done when: Focusing the main action segment of an opted-in split button plays a single streak spanning the full split control, including the chevron segment.
  - Done when: Focusing the chevron segment of an opted-in split button plays a single streak spanning the full split control, including the main action segment.
  - Done when: The streak is not shown as two separate per-segment streaks on the same split control.
- **R4**: A host can start the streak on a button programmatically through a prop whose value change plays one streak, without the button needing to gain focus.
  - Done when: A host can start the streak on a button that is not focused by changing the trigger prop's value.
  - Done when: Every change of the trigger prop's value plays one streak.
  - Done when: The programmatic trigger works whether or not the focus-triggered option is turned on.
